skill.name: twitter-automation
skill.description: Automate Twitter/X actions through the inference.sh belt CLI, including posts, media posts, likes, retweets, direct messages, follows, deletion, and profile lookup.
skill.summary: Run Twitter/X posting and engagement workflows with the belt CLI.
skill.author: skills-shell

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown code spans or code fences, but several documented commands invoke the belt CLI, npx, or remote assets. No prompt injection text was found; the main risks are broad belt command permission and account-mutating Twitter/X automation.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tool patterns to the specific Twitter/X belt commands needed by the skill. Require approval before any nonlisted belt command runs.
Require explicit user confirmation before posting, deleting, liking, retweeting, following, or sending direct messages.

remediation.issue: Unpinned external setup and related skill installs
remediation.suggestion: Pin install references to reviewed versions and explain that related skills are separate trust decisions.
Host marketplace images through a reviewed asset pipeline or remove remote image embeds from the skill file.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Belt CLI Permission Scope
semantic_findings.description: The skill grants Bash access for all belt commands, while the content also encourages browsing the wider app store. This permission is broader than the listed Twitter/X workflows.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools entry permits any belt subcommand, and the skill explicitly references the app store. This creates a clear overbroad permission concern.

semantic_findings.title: Account-Mutating Social Automation
semantic_findings.description: The skill supports posting, likes, retweets, direct messages, follows, and deletion. These actions can affect a connected account and can be abused for spam or unauthorized outreach.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented app list and examples directly include account-changing actions. The risk is contextual business-logic abuse rather than a syntax pattern.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable Twitter/X actions without manual API work. This skill provides belt CLI workflows for posts, media, engagement, messages, follows, and profile lookup.
actual_capabilities: Posts text updates to Twitter/X through the belt CLI.
Creates posts with media URLs when valid media is available.
Likes, retweets, deletes, and retrieves posts by ID.
Sends direct messages with a recipient ID and message text.
Follows users and retrieves user profiles by username.
Shows image and video generation workflows before posting media.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh belt CLI and a configured Twitter/X integration.
Can perform live account actions when commands are approved and run.
Does not verify consent, platform policy compliance, or message quality.
Media posting requires a reachable media URL from a supported source.

use_cases.title: Publish Product Updates
use_cases.description: Prepare and publish approved Twitter/X updates from a repeatable command workflow.

use_cases.title: Manage Engagement Tasks
use_cases.description: Like, retweet, follow, or retrieve posts after reviewing each account action.

use_cases.title: Post Generated Media
use_cases.description: Generate image or video content through belt apps, then create a media post.

prompt_templates.title: Post a Text Update
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single approved post.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use twitter-automation to prepare one Twitter/X post from this message: [message]. Ask for confirmation before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Media Post
prompt_templates.scenario: Add a provided media URL to a post.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Twitter/X media post using this text and media URL: [text] [media URL]. Confirm details before running any command.

prompt_templates.title: Review Engagement Actions
prompt_templates.scenario: Handle likes, retweets, follows, or post lookup.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these target posts and users: [targets]. Recommend safe engagement actions and ask before changing the account.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Generated Media Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using generated media before posting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a workflow that generates media from this brief, captures the media URL, and prepares a Twitter/X post for approval.

output_examples.input: Post a launch update about a new analytics feature.
output_examples.output: A short post draft, an account confirmation request, and the action needed to publish after approval.

output_examples.input: Create a media post for this approved image URL.
output_examples.output: A proposed post caption, a media URL check, and a reminder that publishing changes the connected account.

output_examples.input: Follow this user and send a thank-you message.
output_examples.output: A consent and policy check, a confirmation request, and separate steps for the follow and message actions.

best_practices: Review every post, message, follow, like, retweet, and deletion before approving execution.
Use a dedicated Twitter/X account with limited permissions for automation workflows.
Keep media URLs, recipient IDs, and tweet IDs in an approval record.
anti_patterns: Do not run bulk engagement actions without reviewing targets and platform policy requirements.
Do not send direct messages to users who have not opted in.
Do not install related skills or run broad belt commands without a separate trust review.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It documents belt CLI workflows for Twitter/X posts, media posts, likes, retweets, direct messages, follows, deletion, and profile lookup.

faq.question: Does it require an account connection?
faq.answer: Yes. The belt CLI and the Twitter/X integration must be configured before account actions can run.

faq.question: Can it post media?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create media posts when a supported and reachable media URL is supplied.

faq.question: Can it change my Twitter/X account?
faq.answer: Yes. Posting, deleting, liking, retweeting, following, and sending messages are account-changing actions.

faq.question: Is it safe for bulk outreach?
faq.answer: No. Bulk outreach should be reviewed for consent, platform rules, and brand risk before any command runs.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
